title: Finitude: The One Addition and the Four Pressings

canonical_node.axiom: Creation introduces exactly one new thing: finitude. The attributes of God, pressed through finitude, yield the laws of physics.
definitions: Finitude: a constraint, not a substance; limit, boundary, cost, otherness.
Matter: existence + finitude; bounded, dependent existence.
Space: distinction + finitude; real difference with separation.
Force: relation + finitude; mediated relation requiring a carrier.
Motion: matter + space + force + time together.
Coherence (chi): total integration; the wrapper that holds the four expressions together.
derivation: The Trinity possesses existence, distinction, relation, and orientation infinitely.
Creation introduces finitude as a constraint on these attributes.
Each attribute, when constrained by finitude, produces a physical primitive: existence->matter, distinction->space, relation->force, orientation->time.
These primitives are co-constituted; removing any one collapses the others.
Each attribute generates a family of constraints (laws) with constructive and destructive regimes.
The product form of the ten variables implies a veto property: if any variable goes to zero, the whole collapses.
canonical_node.action: The system should treat finitude as the fundamental creative constraint, deriving physical laws as finite expressions of divine attributes, and use the product form to evaluate coherence (chi) in any bounded system.
boundary: Does not claim to provide a complete derivation of all physical laws; the attribute->law partition is a strong reading, not a derivation (open seam).
Does not specify the mechanism for the L2->L3 fold (consciousness threshold).
Does not claim 'Grace is the only frame-independent quantity' (retracted pending structure).
Does not include the MDA decade-by-decade historical confirmation (excluded by ruling).
test: Check that the four pressings (existence->matter, distinction->space, relation->force, orientation->time) are consistently applied.
Verify that the product form's veto property is used in evaluations (e.g., church health).
Ensure that any claim about electromagnetism's parentage is flagged as unresolved.
Confirm that the build-order test for the nine fruits is pre-registered before scoring data.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a unified framework to derive physical laws from theological attributes via finitude, and a product-form veto for evaluating coherence in systems.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the core theological claims: God's attributes are infinite; creation is finite and dependent; the laws of physics are expressions of divine attributes.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If finitude is removed, the derivation of physical primitives collapses; if the product form is removed, the veto property and the balanced-beats-lopsided argument fail.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Retain as a narrative anchor; flag open seams; do not treat as derivation.

overstatement_risks: Treating the attribute->law partition as a derivation rather than a strong reading.
Claiming the L2->L3 fold is solved when the threshold is unspecified.
Using 'Grace is the only frame-independent quantity' despite retraction.
Assuming the build-order test is valid without pre-registered data.
kill_conditions: If finitude is shown to be insufficient to derive the four primitives.
If the product form is contradicted by empirical evidence.
If the open seams (EM partition, L2->L3 fold) are not resolved or explicitly abandoned.
risk.lean_target: Axiom: Finitude is the sole creative constraint; derivations must be forced, not chosen.

plain_summary: This document proposes that creation introduces finitude as the single new constraint, and that pressing God's attributes through finitude yields matter, space, force, and time, which in turn generate the laws of physics. It outlines a product-form veto for coherence and a staircase from physics to faith, but explicitly flags unresolved seams (electromagnetism partition, consciousness threshold) and retracts a prior claim. It is a coherent theological framework but not a formal derivation.
